coreCurriculum.headline: French 101 Core 30 private pilot
coreCurriculum.threshold: Practice everyday French sentences and explain how regular and irregular verbs work.

lessons.title: Regular -er verbs
lessons.objective: Verbes réguliers en -er : retirer -er et ajouter -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ent : parle, parles, parle, parlons, parlent.

words.en: I study French in the morning.

words.es: Les étudiants pratiquent à la maison.
Est-ce que tu étudies avec nous aujourd'hui ?
words.en: Are you studying with us today?

grammar.focus: Regular -er verbs (parler, étudier, travailler, écouter, pratiquer)

examples.en: I study French in the morning.

steps.instruction: Read Regular -er verbs; explain the French grammar in your own words.
Recall the words and build the lesson sentences, then check and retry.

Role-play Étudier ensemble with a patient classmate. Use regular -er verbs: say J'étudie, tu étudies, nous étudions. Ask Tu étudies avec moi aujourd'hui ? Answer with J'étudie le matin or J'étudie l'après-midi, then ask the partner Tu comprends ? and confirm what they understood. Keep language at beginner level. If the partner asks what a word means, explain it in English.

lessons.title: Regular -er verbs, with irregular exceptions
lessons.objective: Verbes réguliers en -er : retirer -er et ajouter -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ent (manger : mange, manges, mange, mangeons, mangent). Boire, lire et comprendre sont irréguliers et se mémorisent à part.

words.es: Je mange du pain et je bois de l'eau.
words.en: I eat bread and drink water.

words.es: Les amis mangent à la cafétéria.
words.en: The friends eat in the cafeteria.

words.es: Tu bois du café ou de l'eau ?
words.en: Do you drink coffee or water?

grammar.focus: Regular -er verbs (manger), plus irregular boire, lire and comprendre

examples.es: Je mange du pain et je bois de l'eau.
examples.en: I eat bread and drink water.

steps.instruction: Read Regular -er verbs, with irregular exceptions; explain the French grammar in your own words.
Recall the words and build the lesson sentences, then check and retry.

Role-play Le déjeuner with a patient classmate. Use manger and boire: say Je mange, tu manges, nous mangeons, and Je bois, tu bois. Ask Tu bois du café ou de l'eau ? and answer with Je bois de l'eau. Then ask Tu comprends la question ? and confirm the answer. Keep language at beginner level. If the partner asks what a word means, explain it in English.

lessons.title: Regular -ir verbs, with irregular exceptions
lessons.objective: Verbes réguliers en -ir : retirer -ir et ajouter -is, -is, -it, -issons, -issent (finir : finis, finis, finit, finissons, finissent). Vivre, écrire, ouvrir et recevoir sont irréguliers dans cette leçon.

words.en: I live in a small town.

words.es: Nous écrivons des messages en français.
Tu écris à ta famille aujourd'hui ?
words.en: Are you writing to your family today?

grammar.focus: Regular -ir verbs (finir), plus irregular vivre, écrire, ouvrir and recevoir

Use the irregular verbs from the grammar notes: Je vis dans une petite ville, Tu écris à ta famille ? Ask Tu reçois une lettre aujourd'hui ? and confirm the partner's answer. lessons.title: Accord des adjectifs
lessons.objective: Accordez les adjectifs au genre et au nombre du nom : un sac rouge, des sacs rouges, une petite trousse, des petites trousses.

words.en: I am looking for a red backpack.

Recall the words and build the lesson sentences, then check and retry.

Role-play a stationery-shop visit. Ask the sales assistant for a red backpack and two small notebooks. Describe one item with a singular adjective and several items with plural adjectives. Ask where the red backpacks are, answer a related question, and confirm the choice. Use English only to explain a word if requested.

lessons.title: Mon, ton et son
lessons.objective: Choisissez mon, ton ou son selon le genre et le nombre de l'objet possédé, et non selon le propriétaire : mon cahier, ma table, mes livres.

words.es: Mon sac à dos est dans la salle de classe.
words.en: My backpack is in the classroom.

words.es: Mes livres sont dans mon sac à dos.
words.en: My books are in my backpack.

steps.instruction: Read Mon, ton et son; explain the French grammar in your own words.
Recall the words and build the lesson sentences, then check and retry.

Role-play finding things after class. Ask a classmate where their notebook is, tell them their pencils are here, and say where your backpack and books are. Explain that the teacher is looking for her phone and identify where it is. Use mon/ma/mes, ton/ta/tes and son/sa/ses in context.

lessons.title: Avoir : possessions et besoins
lessons.objective: Utilisez avoir au présent pour exprimer ce que l'on possède et certains besoins : j'ai, tu as, il a, nous avons, ils ont ; j'ai faim, elle a soif.

words.es: Nous avons de l'eau dans le sac à dos.

words.es: Mes amis ont le temps de manger.
words.en: My friends have time to eat.

words.es: Tu as un verre pour Ana ?
words.en: Do you have a glass for Ana?

grammar.focus: Present-tense avoir, possession, hunger and thirst

steps.instruction: Read Avoir : possessions et besoins; explain the French grammar in your own words.
Recall the words and build the lesson sentences, then check and retry.

Role-play planning a snack after class. Say that you are hungry, ask whether your partner has water or a glass, and report what Ana, Luis and your friends have. Use j'ai, tu as, il/elle a, nous avons and ils/elles ont, then confirm what the group still needs.

lessons.title: Aller et la contraction au
lessons.objective: Dites où vous allez avec aller au présent et choisissez au, à la, à l’ ou aux selon le lieu.

words.es: Je vais au parc après les cours.
words.en: I am going to the park after class.
Ana is going to the library.

words.es: Nous allons au café à quatre heures.
words.en: We are going to the café at four.
Luis is going to the store.
The friends are going to the cinema.

words.es: Tu vas au parc avec nous ?
words.en: Are you going to the park with us?

grammar.focus: Aller in the present; à + le = au, à + les = aux

examples.es: Je vais au parc après les cours.
examples.en: I am going to the park after class.
Ana is going to the library.

steps.instruction: Read Aller et la contraction au; explain the French grammar in your own words.
Recall the words and build the lesson sentences, then check and retry.

Role-play making plans after class. Ask a friend where they are going, say you are going to the park, and report where Ana, Luis and the group are going. Invite the friend to come with you and agree on four o’clock. Use at least four forms of aller and both au and à la.

lessons.title: Poser des questions : que et quel
lessons.objective: Demandez ce que quelqu’un étudie et choisissez entre des cours ou des livres avec que, quel et lequel en contexte.

words.es: Qu’est-ce que tu étudies ce semestre ?
words.en: What are you studying this semester?

words.es: J’étudie le français et la musique.
Mon cours préféré est le français.

words.en: Which of these books do you prefer?

grammar.focus: Que/quoi for what; quel/quelle for which; lequel for which one

examples.es: Qu’est-ce que tu étudies ce semestre ?
examples.en: What are you studying this semester?

examples.es: J’étudie le français et la musique.

steps.instruction: Read Poser des questions : que et quel; explain the French grammar in your own words.
Recall the words and build the lesson sentences, then check and retry.

Role-play choosing classes with a fellow student. Ask what they study, which class is their favorite, and which of two books they prefer. Answer with French and music, then ask what a word means. Use qu’est-ce que, quel and lequel with their different sentence patterns.

lessons.title: Où, quand et pourquoi
lessons.objective: Posez trois questions distinctes sur le lieu, le moment et la raison, puis répondez avec à, à neuf heures et parce que.

words.es: Le cours commence à neuf heures.
J’étudie le français parce que je veux parler avec mes amis.
words.en: I study French because I want to talk with my friends.

grammar.focus: Où, quand, pourquoi; répondre avec parce que

steps.instruction: Read Où, quand et pourquoi; explain the French grammar in your own words.
Recall the words and build the lesson sentences, then check and retry.

Role-play planning a study session. Ask your friend where they usually study, when class begins and why they study French. Answer with the library, nine o’clock and a reason involving friends. Swap roles and use où, quand, pourquoi and parce que naturally.

grammarNotes.explanation: French -er verbs are regular in most forms. Remove -er to get the stem, then add: je -e, tu -es, il/elle -e, nous -ons, ils/elles -ent. The -ent ending is silent in speech, so ils parlent and il parle sound the same. Étudier follows the same pattern: j'étudie, tu étudies, nous étudions, ils étudient. Note the elision before a vowel: j'étudie, not je étudie.
grammarNotes.caution: Not every -er verb is regular. Aller (je vais) is irregular, and manger changes spelling to mangeons. Lesson 1 uses only regular verbs.

grammarNotes.explanation: Manger is regular but needs an extra e before -ons to keep the soft g sound: nous mangeons. The other forms follow the -er pattern: je mange, tu manges, il mange, ils mangent. Boire, lire and comprendre are NOT regular: boire is je bois, nous buvons; lire is je lis, nous lisons; comprendre is je comprends, nous comprenons, ils comprennent. Learn these as separate patterns.
irregularNotes: boire: je bois, tu bois, il boit, nous buvons, ils boivent
lire: je lis, tu lis, il lit, nous lisons, ils lisent
comprendre (like prendre): je comprends, tu comprends, il comprend, nous comprenons, ils comprennent

grammarNotes.explanation: Regular -ir verbs of the finir type insert -iss- in the plural: nous finissons, ils finissent. Singular forms are je finis, tu finis, il finit. Do NOT apply this pattern to the verbs in this lesson's sentences: vivre (je vis, nous vivons) and écrire (j'écris, nous écrivons) are -re verbs; ouvrir (j'ouvre, nous ouvrons) takes -er-type endings but is irregular; recevoir (je reçois, nous recevons) is irregular. Mark these as exceptions when you learn them.
irregularNotes: vivre: je vis, tu vis, il vit, nous vivons, ils vivent

ouvrir: j'ouvre, tu ouvres, il ouvre, nous ouvrons, ils ouvrent
recevoir: je reçois, tu reçois, il reçoit, nous recevons, ils reçoivent

grammarNotes.explanation: In French, an adjective generally agrees with the noun it describes in gender and number. For many adjectives, add -e for feminine and -s for plural: petit, petite, petits, petites. Rouge already ends in -e, so masculine and feminine singular look alike; the plural is rouges. French adjectives often follow the noun (un sac rouge), though common adjectives such as petit usually precede it (un petit cahier). Spoken final -s is normally silent.
grammarNotes.caution: The article also changes with the noun: un sac, une trousse, des sacs. Not every adjective forms its feminine simply by adding -e.

grammarNotes.explanation: French has several ways to ask what or which; choose the form that fits the sentence. Use qu’est-ce que before a full clause: Qu’est-ce que tu étudies ? Use quel/quelle before a noun: Quel cours préfères-tu ? Quelle est ta matière préférée ? For ‘which one of these books,’ use lequel before de ces livres. Que signifie ce mot ? is a concise way to ask what a word means. In speech, est-ce que questions are common and do not require inversion.

grammarNotes.caution: Quel agrees with the noun: quel cours, quelle matière, quels livres, quelles classes. Lequel can stand for a selected item; it is not interchangeable with quel before a noun.
